Note: London to York and on to Berwick and Scotland; the road of kings and armies (Towton and Barnet lie on it)

Name: Watling Street and the Chester road
Note: Roman Watling Street to Towcester then the medieval road by Coventry to Chester

Name: The road to Carlisle
Note: The west road north (drawn on the Gough Map)

Name: Watling Street (Dover road)
Note: Pilgrims to Canterbury and the crossing to Calais

Name: Sandwich road
Note: To the port of Sandwich

Name: The Bristol road
Note: London to the second port of England

Name: The Oxford and Gloucester road
Note: Through the Cotswold wool country

Name: The March road
Note: Along the Welsh March: Hereford; Ludlow (Duke of York); Shrewsbury; Chester

Name: The Winchester road
Note: To Winchester and the port of Southampton

Name: The western road
Note: London to Salisbury and the West Country (Devon part not in the first release)

Name: The Norwich road
Note: London to Norwich and the herring port of Yarmouth

Name: The Cambridge and Lynn road
Note: Roman Ermine Street to Royston; then Cambridge; Ely and Lynn

Note: The Roman road from the south-west to Lincoln; by 1455 a main road, not a great highway along its whole length

Name: The Severn road
Note: Up the Severn valley

Name: The Tyne Gap road
Note: Across the north along Hadrian's Wall

Note: Roman road over Stainmore to the west; passes near Middleham

Name: The Nottingham road
Note: Through the East Midlands

Name: The Aire Gap road
Note: Across the Pennines through the Aire gap

Name: Stane Street
Note: The Roman road from London to Chichester

Name: The Somerset road
Note: Bristol to Wells, Glastonbury and Bridgwater, on to the West Country (Devon part not in the first release)

Name: The Wensleydale road
Note: Up to the Neville country: Ripon, Masham, Middleham and Richmond

Name: The Bury road
Note: The other road to Norwich, by Newmarket, Bury St Edmunds and Thetford

Name: The wool road
Note: Through the Suffolk cloth country

Name: The Banbury road
Note: Oxford to Banbury, Warwick and Coventry

Name: The Boston road
Note: Lincoln to the wool port of Boston

Name: The Whitby road
Note: Over the moors to Whitby

Name: The Rye road
Note: London to the Cinque port of Rye
